summary: A ~150,000 sq ft community center at 1675 Owens St housing the Bakar Fitness & Recreation Center, the Mission Bay Conference Center, administrative offices and a restaurant/food court, opened 2005 as part of Mission Bay's first development phase in Legorreta's contemporary Mexican-modernist style.

milestones.text: UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings certifies a CEQA EIR addendum and approves the design of the Mission Bay Campus Community Center Building (21B) -- this building, confirmed by matching architects (MBT Architecture as executive architect with Legorreta Arquitectos as design subconsultant) and program (fitness/recreation center, conference center, food service, retail); a $58,000,000 total project budget was approved in March 2000, with construction slated for 2001-2002
William J. Rutter Community Center opens

costs.what: Total project budget the UC Regents approved in March 2000 for the Mission Bay Campus Community Center Building (21B), confirmed as this building by matching architects and program, per the May 2000 Regents design-approval item that recounts the budget action

facts.value: Legorreta Arquitectos (Ricardo and Victor Legorreta), with MBT Architecture as associate/executive architect
Bakar Fitness & Recreation Center, Mission Bay Conference Center, administrative offices, restaurant/food court

images.caption: William J. Rutter Center
images.appeal_note: Clear daytime shot of the Rutter Center's brick-and-glass facade under blue sky, but the foreground lawn is busy with an outdoor event -- a small crowd, tents and flags -- rather than a clean approach shot.

images.credit: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Farm Service Agency, NAIP aerial imagery (2024 flight), via USDA's 'latest NAIP' image service
images.license_note: USDA's data.gov catalog record for NAIP imagery sets the license to the U.S. government public-domain label (usa.gov/publicdomain/label/1.0); the USDA FSA policies page says public-domain information may be freely distributed with credit requested ('U.S. Department of Agriculture, Farm Service Agency'). Read 2026-09-22.
images.caption: USDA NAIP aerial orthophoto (2024 flight), cropped to the Mission Bay project area and its immediate surroundings
images.appeal_note: A straight-down orthophoto rather than an oblique aerial, but Oracle Park and Chase Center are both clearly recognizable landmarks in the frame, giving anyone who knows the city an immediate fix on the neighborhood.

images.credit: Firstcultural (Alfred Twu), aerial view from a departing flight, via Wikimedia Commons; CC0; downscaled to 1600 px
images.license_note: Wikimedia Commons' license box on the file page confirms CC0 (public domain dedication) by Firstcultural (Alfred Twu). Read 2026-09-23.
images.caption: Aerial view of Mission Bay, Oracle Park and the Caltrain/King Street area from a departing flight
images.appeal_note: Oracle Park's diamond and Chase Center's dome (with its own logo) are both clearly identifiable landmarks in one colorful frame -- reads far better at card size than the flatter government orthophoto.
